program: Community medical, dental and related care
priceScope: Whole recognized expense; oral-surgery-only conditional benefit; donor HOLD

what: TOMAGWA provides medical, dental, vision, pharmacy and related care for people with limited resources around Tomball and greater Houston.
It became a federally qualified health center look-alike in 2024 and serves uninsured patients alongside Medicare and Medicaid patients.
Federal reporting identifies 118 oral-surgery patients in 2024; other services are not included in this narrow health illustration.
strengths: Original filings and federal data identify the recipient, whole recognized spending and a defined surgery cohort.
Patient ZIP data and the recipient's needs assessment document substantial Houston-metro reach.
An official one-time and recurring donation route exists.
reservations: A gift-created surgery and measurable additional pain relief are unverified; existing dental grants may replace ordinary gifts.
2024 accounts are unaudited and unrecognized volunteer-service costs are unknown.
The QALY bridge is judgment-based and partial; it does not demonstrate whole-organization cost effectiveness.

sections.what: TOMAGWA provides comprehensive primary and dental care, pharmacy, vision, laboratory and case-management services. Current locations include Tomball and Champions in Houston, with mobile delivery across Greater Houston and Harris County. Its 2024 Form 990 identifies TOMAGWA Ministries Inc DBA TOMAGWA HealthCare Ministries, EIN 76-0280324, and February 2024 FQHC Look-Alike designation. Look-Alike status is not proof of federal Section 330 funding. [Recipient site](https://www.tomagwa.org/) [Original filing](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202503219349321450/IRS990)
sections.monitoring: The 2024 HRSA return counts 1,965 patients overall and 118 oral-surgery patients with 131 surgery visits (Table6A DJ97 and DI97). In 2025 the corresponding surgery counts are 135 patients and 240 visits. These are reported treatment-category patients, not observed incremental cures. Restorative and examination patients can overlap and receive no added modeled credit. The 2024 tax filing repeats a 2023 narrative of 18,326 dental services; that is neither 2024 activity nor a unique-patient count. [2024 UDS](https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/StaticDocuments/LAL-2024.xlsx) [2025 UDS](https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/StaticDocuments/LAL-2025.xlsx)
sections.qualitative: Care reaches a population with limited resources and plausible unmet need. The 2024 federal ZIP rows place 1,758 patients in named Houston-metro ZIP areas; 28 are in Plantersville/Grimes, 156 in other ZIPs, and some small cells are suppressed. This is overall patient residence, not surgery-specific health attribution. A Swedish prospective cohort compared root canals with extraction and found no significant intergroup QALY difference; it does not identify the benefit of TOMAGWA surgery over alternative care. The model therefore labels utility, relief and duration as priors. [Needs assessment](https://www.tomagwa.org/_files/ugd/a79649_a42ddabd7ed84d0ca420cfde6c9a8ff0.pdf) [Clinical study](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cre2.759)
sections.cost:
Whole FY2024 recognized expenses were $2,471,560, including program, administration, fundraising and $113,318 reported medical-supplies expense; the matching donated supplies must not be added again. The filing reports no audit, and 2024 volunteer-service valuation is unknown. Dividing this whole expense by only a hypothetical surgery-pain benefit produces a central $43.8 million per 10 Houston QALYs, with null and harm cases retained. Other clinical benefits remain unestimated. This is a historical partial-health illustration, not a marginal gift price or complete organizational ranking. [Original filing](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202503219349321450/IRS990) [Schedule M](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202503219349321450/IRS990ScheduleM)

An explicit missing-resource case adds a hypothetical $476,624 of volunteer/service costs (the prior year's adjustment, not an observed 2024 value), raising the conditional price to about $52.2 million per ten QALYs. An isolated zero-funding-response case preserves the other central clinical assumptions but yields zero gift-created health. Unmeasured other-portfolio benefits may be positive or negative; this narrow illustration is not a proven lower bound.
sections.funding: Donor HOLD. TRHF approved $595,000 of 2024 dental funding and described a $400,000 February–December 2025 contract; these are existing funding, not open gift gaps. UDS also reports local government and private grants. Current clinician capacity, 2026 grant renewal, restrictions and the response to a new gift need verification. The official giving form permits ordinary gifts but prices no additional surgery. [2024 funding approval](https://trhfoundation.org/images/pdfs/financials/minutes/20231129_THA_Board_Minutes_Signed.pdf) [2025 contract minutes](https://trhfoundation.org/2025-board-minutes/158-february-19-2025-1) [Give](https://www.tomagwa.org/donate)

model.costScope: Whole FY2024 recognized organizational expenses; includes medical supplies already recognized. Unrecognized volunteer costs remain unknown. Narrow surgery-only health illustration, not full portfolio or marginal gift price.
model.geographicAttribution: 2024 ZIP rows and CHNA county mapping establish actual Houston reach. Central 93% benefit share is a judgment; surgical cohort geography is unknown and some ZIP areas cross counties.
model.formula: benefit = patients * symptomaticSuccessfulShare * incrementalRelief * utility * years; allPopulationQalys = (benefit - harmQalys) * fundingResponse; editionQalys = allPopulationQalys * houstonShare; pricePer10 = 10 * costUSD / positive editionQalys
model.counterfactual: Other dental providers, public/payer coverage and existing TRHF contracts can substitute for ordinary-gift support. Symptom success, additional relief and funding response are separately explicit priors.
model.attribution: Whole-recipient expense retained; one annual surgery-patient cohort only. No double credit for exams/restorations or partners. Other programs remain unestimated.
model.uncertainty: Very low confidence in health and donation attribution. Scenarios are illustrative, not confidence intervals; no calibrated probabilities or expected-value estimate. Null and adverse are viable.
model.nativeOutcomes: Reported oral-surgery patients, discounted for symptomatic successful treatment and relief beyond alternative care, with finite utility duration and harm.

inputs.name: Whole recognized expense
inputs.rationale: Part IX total includes all three functional categories; $113318 supply expense not added twice. Volunteer valuation unknown.

inputs.name: patients
inputs.rationale: Table6A DJ97; not 131 visits, not 18326 historical services.

inputs.name: symptomaticSuccessfulShare
inputs.rationale: Share with a symptomatic problem and successful treatment; not an observed local completion or outcome rate.

inputs.name: incrementalRelief
inputs.rationale: Relief remaining after alternative care and spontaneous symptom change; unmeasured.

inputs.name: utility
inputs.rationale: Explicit utility prior; study does not supply this effect.

inputs.name: years
inputs.rationale: Finite three-month duration relative to counterfactual; no lifetime gain credited.

inputs.name: harmQalys
inputs.rationale: Aggregate treatment/complication/functional loss allowance; adverse case permits net harm.

inputs.name: fundingResponse
inputs.rationale: Proxy response after funding substitution and capacity limits; not observed gift elasticity.

inputs.name: houstonShare
inputs.rationale: All-patient residence supports local care but not a measured surgery-specific health share.

scenarios.label: Gift completely substitutes for existing resources

sensitivity: Unrecognized donated-service sensitivity adds a hypothetical $476624 (the observed 2023 amount, not a 2024 observation) to 2024 cost, increasing every positive price by 19.28%.
Funding response of zero yields no incremental health regardless of service counts.
The 2025 count of 135 surgery patients is contextual; do not combine it with 2024 costs and call that an observed same-year ratio.
The hypothetical central benefit cannot establish the overall value of a broad clinical recipient whose other health pathways remain unestimated.

2024 unrecognized volunteer services and complete resource reconciliation
Surgery case mix and measured pain/function outcomes
Quantified benefits and overlaps across other clinical programs
